findings.title: Missing prisma import causes ReferenceError
findings.body: File packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts calls prisma.credential.update at line 96 but never imports prisma. Any execution of getClient will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking all Salesforce operations after this PR.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce connection still uses expired token
findings.body: File packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts fetches a new access token into accessTokenParsed but then constructs jsforce.Connection with accessToken: credentialKey.access_token and instanceUrl from the old credential. The refresh is persisted but never used, so calls continue with the expired token and will keep failing.

findings.title: Minimum token schema uses invalid computed keys
findings.body: File packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts defines minimumTokenResponseSchema with computed keys [z.string().toString()]. That evaluates to a literal property name like the stringified Zod object, not a catch-all. The schema does not mean access_token plus any expiry field; it requires a nonsense property. Use z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough() or catchall instead. As written sync-mode validation will reject valid provider responses or accept wrong shapes.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites real refresh token
findings.body: File packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts mutates parsed data with refresh_token = "refresh_token" when missing. Callers like Office365 spread tokenResponse.data over stored credentials, so the real refresh_token is permanently replaced by the literal string "refresh_token". Subsequent normal refreshes will fail and the credential is corrupted.

findings.title: Stores SafeParse wrapper instead of credential key
findings.body: File packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts assigns const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...) which returns a Zod SafeParse result {success, data}. It then stores that wrapper as prisma.credential key. Previously it stored googleCredentialSchema.parse output directly. Stored Google credentials will now be {success:true, data:{...}} instead of token fields, breaking googleCredentialSchema.parse on next load.

findings.title: Sync path returns raw fetch Response incompatible with callers
findings.body: File packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns a raw fetch Response when credential sync is enabled, but callers expect different shapes: Google expects res.data, HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object, Lark/Office365 expect fetch or axios responses with specific helpers. For example Google does res?.data then token.access_token which will be undefined for a fetch Response, and HubSpot stores the Response object as the credential key. The abstraction leaks provider-specific response types and breaks refresh when enabled. It also never checks response.ok or parses JSON.

findings.title: Unhandled validation/decrypt errors and missing method check
findings.body: File apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse without try/catch and accepts any HTTP method. Invalid body, wrong encryption key, or non-JSON payload throws uncaught and returns 500 instead of 400, and GET requests can hit the endpoint. A maintainer would want method restriction to POST and proper 400 handling.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as userId to sync endpoint
findings.body: File packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts calls refreshOAuthTokens with credentialId as the third argument, but that parameter is userId and is sent as calcomUserId. The sync endpoint will receive the credential row id instead of the Cal.com user id, so it cannot resolve the correct user tokens. Should pass credential.userId like other integrations.

findings.title: Sync refresh overwrites credential with partial token
findings.body: File packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts stores the sync-endpoint responseBody directly as the credential key. When sync is enabled the endpoint returns only access_token/expiry, so email, refresh_token, scope and other fields are deleted from the DB. The code also derives expiry_date from expires_in which will be missing, yielding Date.now() and immediate expiry. This permanently loses the refresh token.

findings.title: Wrong appSlug sent to credential sync endpoint
findings.body: File packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts calls refreshOAuthTokens with appSlug "zoomvideo" while the credential is created with appId "zoom". The sync endpoint keyed by appSlug will not match, so Zoom refresh via sync will fail or update the wrong app. Should be "zoom" for consistency with other adapters that send appId.
